tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. entries.name: WebFetch
entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

## Release and Announcement

Funcom's April 2026 Developer Update confirmed private, self-hosted dedicated servers for Dune: Awakening. Self-hosted servers are finally coming to the game, which represents a significant change as the game ran exclusively on Funcom's official servers with no way to spin up your own private slice of Arrakis previously.

## How Self-Hosting Works

Self-hosting is a way for users to host Dune Awakening Worlds on their own machines and connect to them, with hosts able to tweak various settings in configuration files to change the behavior of the game servers.

## Technical Requirements

The initial version requires Windows Pro with Hyper-V, with additional options to be explored later. Hagga Basin will be capped at 40 concurrent players, but you could technically host your own World with multiple Sietches, though most people are expected to be capped to 1 Sietch or 40 players concurrently.

## Cost

Funcom will not charge players additional money for this feature but you may incur additional costs depending on your agreement with your Internet Service Provider.

I found information about Dune: Awakening Self-Hosted Server on Steam. Here are the key details:

## Overview
It is now possible to self-host an entire Dune: Awakening world on your own hardware. Self-Hosted Servers are currently in an early iteration, and will become more accessible over time with testing and feedback. This is still an early iteration of the tool and will change over time following wider community testing and feedback.

## Requirements
After enabling hardware virtualization on their BIOS and turning the HyperV feature on, users will be able to download the Dune: Awakening Self-Hosted Server product on Steam and begin the process.

## Setup Process
In the program files you will find a battlegroup.bat file. Running it as administrator will show various options for setting up and running a battlegroup. Initial-setup will guide you through a series of choices in order to prepare the VM's network and resources as needed, and setting up the battlegroup in kubernetes.

## Port Requirements
You will need to port forward the following ports: 7777-7810 UDP for the game servers. 31982 TCP For RMQ.

## Server Configuration
By opening the file browser, hosts will find a UserSettings folder with user ini config files that allow them to change the behavior of the servers in the battlegroup. Some options are documented for them to change, but they are able to create various other User ini files to manipulate any exposed setting.

content.content: Hello Sleepers, Today we rolled out our first iteration of Self-Hosted Servers. This is a more complex process than in some other games, one of the main reasons we wanted to get an early iteration out was to test it live with our community, so we can shape the tool around the way you actually want to play. At its core, this feature lets you host your own World containing the servers that run the game’s maps from Hagga Basin to Deep Desert and everything in between. With the current functionality you can already adapt the game to your liking, including things like full PvP servers, adjusted gathering rates, disabling the Sandworm, or changing building limits. This is your World; you can have it all to yourself or share it with whoever you want. You can get the full instructions here: https://duneawakening.com/self-hosted-servers/We're also hosting a livestream tomorrow at 17:00 CEST / 11AM EDT / 8AM PDT, where Michael Søvik, our Tools and DevOps Director, and Joel Bylos, Creative Director, will walk you through the setup process and answer any questions you have. This will be live on our Twitch channel here. Longer term, we're looking to open up more settings and improve the overall experience, both in hosting and the in-game admin tools. Your feedback is crucial to that process. We've already taken a lot of notes from PTC testers and are looking forward to hearing more. The best place to share feedback is our Discord, in the Technical channel under the Game Discussion category. Stay safe, Sleepers.

## Server Limit for Game Licenses

Each Hytale game license can authenticate up to 100 concurrent servers. If you need more, you can purchase additional licenses or apply for a Game Server Provider account.

## For Game Server Providers

The Server Provider Authentication Guide explains how server hosting providers can authenticate Hytale dedicated servers. For Game Server Providers and server network operators wanting automatic 0-click server authentication for up-to 500 servers, you can obtain tokens once using the Device Code Flow to authenticate and get a refresh_token, then create sessions and pass tokens to servers for automatic authentication.

If you're a hosting provider running many servers, you can apply for the sessions.unlimited_servers entitlement which removes the 100-server limit by contacting Hytale Support with your company details.

## Token Management

The server stays authenticated indefinitely as long as it remains online. Re-authentication is only required if the server is offline for longer than the refresh token TTL (30 days).

The official Server Provider Authentication Guide is available through Hytale's support documentation at support.hytale.com for more detailed technical implementation information.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Arma Reforger dedicated server setup with SteamCMD:

## Key Information

The dedicated server is a separate SteamCMD application (app ID 1874900) that installs anonymously — you log in to SteamCMD as anonymous and no game ownership is checked on the host machine.

## Linux Setup

Bohemia ships a genuine native Linux binary, ./ArmaReforgerServer — no compatibility layer is needed. Linux dependencies typically include libcurl4 and libssl (often libssl1.1), and optionally net-tools for diagnostics.

## SteamCMD Installation Command

For Linux, a typical installation command would be:
`steamcmd +login anonymous +force_install_dir /home/steam/arma-reforger +app_update 1874900 validate +quit`

## Ports Required

Open UDP ports: 2001 (game socket) and 17777 (Steam/A2S query).

The search results confirm that app ID 1874900 is the correct stable dedicated server application for Arma Reforger and supports both Windows and Linux installation through SteamCMD with anonymous login.

I found search results related to your query about Arma 3 server setup with SteamCMD and app 233780. Here's what the search results show:

**Key Finding - Conflicting Information:**

There's conflicting information about anonymous login for Arma 3 server app 233780:

App 233780 (Arma 3 Dedicated Server) requires a Steam account that owns Arma 3. An anonymous session fails with "No subscription" and exit code 8. Plenty of older guides say otherwise; they are out of date, and it is the single most common reason a first install stops dead.

However, another source states: The dedicated server package downloads through SteamCMD with `login anonymous`, so no game license is required on the host. You only need the game on the machines that will actually play.

**Account Requirements:**

The account used to login must own a valid copy of Arma 3. If you're using a named Steam account, it needs to have Arma 3 purchased.

The conflicting information suggests that while some sources indicate anonymous login should work, more recent guidance (July 2026) indicates it will fail with a "No subscription" error and requires a Steam account that owns Arma 3.

Neither Grounded nor Grounded 2 has official dedicated servers. Grounded 2 ships with stock 4-player peer-to-peer online co-op only - no official dedicated server tooling exists.

## Current Multiplayer Implementation

Instead of dedicated servers, the co-op gameplay supports four players per session using peer-to-peer connectivity rather than dedicated servers. Grounded uses a "shared world" function. When authorized players join, they host the world using peer-to-peer connection.

## Future Possibilities

The original Grounded launched with peer-to-peer hosting first and added proper dedicated server support later in its life cycle, and Obsidian has signaled that Grounded 2 is being built with lessons from the first game's community feedback, with self-hosted dedicated servers being one of the most requested features carried over from Grounded 1's community.

While official support is unavailable, third-party hosting services use an open-source Lantern framework where friends join through the Lantern launcher, and the backyard runs 24/7 even when nobody is logged in.

Due to Windows having a 1024 character limit on command line arguments and the token being a fairly long JSON Web Token, you can use the environment variable AG_AUTH_TOKEN instead.

I found information about setting up a VEIN dedicated server on Linux using SteamCMD with anonymous login.

The dedicated server installs through SteamCMD with anonymous login — no Steam account required. Use 2131400, the dedicated-server app, with SteamCMD and anonymous login.

For Linux specifically, Linux is supported (Ubuntu 20.04+). Run steamcmd +force_install_dir (directory) +login anonymous +app_update 2131400 validate +quit to install Vein server files.

Key configuration details:
- The official wiki specifies game port UDP 7777 and query port UDP 7778 ("always +2 of the game port").
- The VEIN dedicated server is a headless Unreal Engine 5 tool that runs without a GPU. It is mainly CPU-bound, so plan for roughly 2 to 4 cores and 8 to 16 GB of RAM on a box that stays online 24/7.
- Launch the server once so it generates its files, then edit Game.ini in Vein/Saved/Config (LinuxServer or WindowsServer).

## BeamMP AuthKey Overview

Every BeamMP server requires an Auth Key to function, which links your server to your BeamMP account via the Keymaster dashboard. A BeamMP AuthKey is required for your server to appear in the public server browser.

## Keymaster Access and Key Generation

You can generate one for free through the BeamMP Keymaster website using your Discord account. By default, every Discord account registered on the Keymaster is provided with two (2) keys for hosting.

## Key Limitations and Expansion

You have a limited number of keys, and one key can be used on one server at a time, so you cannot start two servers at the same time with the same key. You can increase your limit by supporting the BeamMP Project on Patreon.

## Commercial Hosting Partners

It is recommended to host a server with one of BeamMP's partnered services. ## Key Information

To download the dedicated server files (App ID 1424230), you can use: `steamcmd.sh +login anonymous +force_install_dir /opt/holdfastserver +app_update 1424230 +quit`

The game offers an anonymous dedicated server for both Linux and Windows.

## Important Notes

- The dedicated server App ID is 1424230 (not 589290, the game client).
- For Linux, you need to allow UDP ports 20100, 8700, and 27000 through your firewall using: `sudo ufw allow 20100/udp sudo ufw allow 8700/udp sudo ufw allow 27000/udp sudo ufw reload`
- You can launch the server on Linux using the provided launch script: LaunchServer.sh
- To allow other players to connect, you must configure port forwarding on your router and open the necessary UDP ports in your local firewall.

# MotorTown Behind The Wheel Dedicated Server Plugin

## Key Technical Details

**Steam App ID:** The dedicated server uses app ID 2223650, while the game itself is app ID 1369670.

**Login Requirements:** The setup requires a Steam account with credentials. During installation, users must "Generate a token for your game server" via the Steam Community developer portal. A Game Server Login Token (GSLT) is needed and placed in the WGSM configuration.

**Platform:** Windows only—the plugin is designed for WindowsGSM on Windows systems. Server files are downloaded via SteamCMD and require specific DLL files from the Steam installation directory.

**Configuration Timeline:** After initial installation, users must run the game client first to generate the configuration file, then edit `DedicatedServerConfig.json` before launching the dedicated server.

**Notable Constraint:** "max\_players this can't be more than 100 ish I think <=was hardcoded from what I picked up in the community."

The project is currently in alpha/beta stages with ongoing development for features like a web interface for REST API functionality.

# Aska Dedicated Server Docker Installation Overview

## Server Installation Method
The Docker container utilizes SteamCMD to download and install the Aska dedicated server. The setup requires creating an authentication token for AppId `1898300` from Steam's Manage Game Servers portal before deployment.

## Wine Integration
The implementation leverages the pterodactyl/wine yolk base image from Ptero-Eggs. According to the documentation: "This image uses the pterodactyl/wine yolk Ptero-Eggs as it was the only thing working." The Windows emulation layer enables running the server on Linux, though the maintainers note that "the volume paths are not that great since it uses the windows emulation."

## Authentication Requirements
Users must obtain a Steam authentication token prior to deployment. The README specifies: "You need to create the authentication token for AppId `1898300` from the Steam Manage-Game-Servers site."

## Known Issues
The project identifies several operational challenges:
- Servers disconnect after minutes without active players (partially addressed via keep-alive detection)
- Savegame IDs reset upon restart, creating duplicate saves (users can specify a SAVE_ID variable to mitigate this)
- Lingering Wine/Xvfb compatibility issues requiring user bug reports for resolution

The documentation warns: "If anything is wrong with the config the Aska server will just crash," emphasizing configuration sensitivity.

# Among Us Mod Policy: Private Servers, Monetization & Commercial Use

## Private Servers & Commissioned Mods

Innersloth permits private commissioned mods. They state: **"A mod that is commissioned and funded by you and your friends for private use among those players only."** is acceptable.

For exclusive gameplay features, they clarify: **"Yes – accepting commissions to create any type of mod (gameplay or cosmetic) is acceptable!"**

## Charging Money / Monetization

Innersloth discourages but technically permits charging for gameplay mods:

**"A mod that provides gameplay features, but requires a donation or active subscription to function... is technically permitted, but discouraged."**

However, they emphasize: **"It is our goal to provide all additional gameplay features in Among Us free of cost."**

## Key Monetization Limits

- ✅ **Allowed:** Donation buttons, Patreon supporters, modest prices on distribution sites
- ⚠️ **Discouraged:** Gameplay behind paywalls/subscriptions
- ❌ **Prohibited:** Advertisements or monetization features within Among Us itself

They note: **"We cannot be held accountable for any bugs or complaints as a result of your mod or its monetization."**

## Not viable for Nxeon

- **Arma 3 (233780):** needs a Steam login. LinuxGSM marks it login-only; https://billet.gg/guides/arma-3-dedicated-server-steamcmd (July 2026) says the account must own Arma 3. Demand is 8,234 / 56,185.
- **Starbound (211820):** needs a login and a purchase ([LGSM], [AMP:starbound]).
- **Assetto Corsa Competizione (1430110):** needs a login ([AMP:assetto-corsa-comp]); Windows only, runs under Wine. Demand 3,569.
- **Assetto Corsa EVO (4564210):** self-hosted server arrived with v0.6 in April 2026, but "you MUST own" the game (https://support.505games.com/support/solutions/articles/150000225040-assetto-corsa-evo-dedicated-server-setup). Windows only; runs under Proton.
- **Motor Town (2223650):** anonymous login fails, you must own the game; Windows only (https://steamcommunity.com/app/1369670/discussions/0/758394056999985884/, forum posts Jan–Apr 2025; current 2026 status unverified).
- **Aloft (1660080):** "A steam account that owns the game is required" (https://eggs.pterodactyl.io/egg/games-aloft).
- **Farming Simulator 25:** not on SteamCMD. You need a separate game license per server, and the Steam version can't run in Docker. Windows only; runs under Wine. 10 official partners. Demand 44,205 / 135,883 (https://github.com/wine-gameservers/arch-fs25server, https://www.farming-simulator.com/fs25-rent-a-dedicated-server.php).
- **Chivalry 2:** Nitrado is the only host; Torn Banner says it has no plans to add other partners (https://chivalry2.com/2024/03/15/chivalry-2-unofficial-servers-faq-follow-up/).
- **Deadside:** server files not released; G-Portal only (https://steamcommunity.com/app/895400/discussions/0/4300317606647568450/).
- **Medieval Dynasty:** "no plans currently for dedicated servers" (Dec 2023, https://steamcommunity.com/app/1129580/discussions/0/4030222834111241429/).
- **Grounded 2** and **Subnautica 2:** no official servers. Rival hosts sell them through unofficial frameworks ("Lantern" for Grounded 2, "Beacon" for Subnautica 2).
- **Pacific Drive:** single-player only; its Steam listing has no multiplayer categories.
- **Stormforge:** early access 10 Nov 2026. The self-host claim comes only from a third party (https://low.ms/blog/stormforge-server-hosting-early-access-preview); I haven't confirmed it officially. Worth watching.

## Other findings

- A text search of `/opt/nxeon/lib` suggests Dragonwilds, Soulmask, Abiotic Factor, Enshrouded, Icarus, Terraria, Vintage Story, Core Keeper and Necesse are already in the catalog, so I didn't list them as new. Among "Minecraft-likes", Hytale is the only big new one.
- The best mix of demand and fit with Nxeon's anonymous-download rule: Arma Reforger, SCUM, Bannerlord, BeamMP, Assetto Corsa through AssettoServer, and CS 1.6. Dune and Hytale have bigger upside but come with token and authentication overhead.
